learningObjectives: Define the responsibilities of key roles in Pega project delivery
Match each role to the studio(s) they use
Explain how Workspaces and Branches enable isolated parallel development
Monitor Branch health with Branch quality metrics

elements.term: Delivery roles: PO, Project Manager, Scrum Master
elements.description: PRODUCT OWNER — manages scope and prioritizes sprint requirements. PROJECT MANAGER — leads delivery, maintains governance, liaises with client leadership. SCRUM MASTER — runs Sprint ceremonies (Planning, Sizing, Backlog Refinement, Retrospectives) and removes impediments.

elements.text: Developing a Pega application as a team is like building a house with specialists working simultaneously: the architect draws plans (SA), the electrician wires rooms while the plumber installs pipes (parallel development), and each team works from a locked blueprint version (Ruleset version). Without the version lock, one team could accidentally overwrite another's work.

elements.term: Build & quality roles: SA/SSA/LSA, QA, BA
elements.description: SYSTEM ARCHITECTS (SA/SSA/LSA) configure the application — LSA imports Blueprint files. QUALITY ANALYSTS verify requirements and write test scripts. BUSINESS ARCHITECT translates business needs into workflows, Data Models, and user experiences.

elements.term: Client & design roles: SME, UX, Solutions Consultant
elements.description: SUBJECT MATTER EXPERT — client operational expert who supplies requirements. UX DESIGNER — ensures design meets user needs and accessibility standards. SOLUTIONS CONSULTANT — engages client in sales, co-designs Blueprint, hands off to delivery team.

APP STUDIO (no-code) serves SAs, BAs, UX designers, solutions consultants, Project Managers, and Scrum Masters. DEV STUDIO (advanced) serves SAs and QAs. PREDICTION STUDIO serves data scientists. ADMIN STUDIO serves business IT for administration.

elements.description: Parallel development flows through three scopes: a WORKSPACE holds one developer's PRIVATE changes; a BRANCH holds the TEAM's changes; the APPLICATION holds the GENERALLY AVAILABLE features. Changes promote outward: Workspace → Branch → Application.

Private development space tied to one operator and one application. Changes stay isolated until shared to a Branch — avoiding rule conflicts. Each operator gets one Workspace by default; multiple are allowed. Enabled via the EnableWorkspace setting.

A BRANCH is a container of Rulesets under active development. Branch Rulesets are based on (branched from) another Ruleset. Best practice: one Branch per feature so teams work in isolation — a finished feature merges independently.

A Branch merges into the main application only after the feature is complete, conflicts are resolved, and approval is granted. Pega automatically checks which Rules are new or updated before completing the merge.

elements.description: Settings that flag elements not complying with Pega best practices. You must respond to warnings to keep the application efficient. The WEIGHTED SCORE metric reflects the number and severity of guardrail warnings on a Branch.
(1) GUARDRAILS — weighted score. (2) MERGE CONFLICTS — total conflicts. (3) TEST COVERAGE & UNIT TESTS — rules covered % and pass rate %. (4) UNCOVERED RULES — Branch Rules not covered by any test.

elements.title: Studio & Role Assignment Decisions

examPitfalls.title: Role responsibilities
examPitfalls.trapDescription: PO = scope + sprint priorities; Project Manager = governance/liaison; Scrum Master = ceremonies + removes impediments; LSA imports Blueprint; Solutions Consultant co-designs the Blueprint early in sales.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Match each responsibility to the right role — these are common scenario questions.

examPitfalls.title: Roles ↔ studios
examPitfalls.trapDescription: App Studio serves most roles (PM docs, Scrum user stories); Dev Studio serves SAs + QAs; Prediction Studio = data scientists; Admin Studio = IT.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Map each team role to its primary Studio: SA/LSA use Dev Studio for technical work; Citizen Developers and BAs use App Studio for configuration.

examPitfalls.title: Workspace = one operator, one application
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A Workspace is private to one operator and one app (one by default, can create multiple); changes stay private until shared to a Branch.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Enable the Workspace feature (EnableWorkspace setting) before use; assign each developer a private Workspace to prevent rule conflicts during parallel feature development.

examPitfalls.title: Branch Rulesets
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask where new rules created during parallel development are stored. Candidates say 'the main application Ruleset.' Rules created during team development are stored in Branch Rulesets — they are merged back into the main Ruleset when the branch is complete.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Create a Branch Ruleset per feature or developer to isolate work — merge back into the main Ruleset only after the feature is complete, conflict-free, and approved.

examPitfalls.title: Merge prerequisites
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A Branch merges into the main application only after the feature is complete, conflicts are resolved, and approval is granted.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Don't merge until complete + conflict-free + approved; the system auto-checks updated/new Rules.

examPitfalls.title: Branch quality metrics
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The four metrics are Guardrails (Weighted score), Merge conflicts (Total), Test coverage/Unit tests (Rules covered %, Test pass rate %), and Uncovered Rules.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Review all four Branch quality metrics before merging: Guardrails weighted score, Merge conflicts total, Test coverage percentage, and Approval status — all must pass.

examPitfalls.title: Parallel development requires locked Ruleset versions
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question describes a team starting parallel development and asks what must be done first. Candidates say 'create a branch.' Before branching, the current Ruleset version must be locked — an unlocked Ruleset cannot be branched safely because the base is still in flux.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: For safe parallel development, Rulesets must be locked at specific versions before branching. Each team works on their own version or branch application. Without version control, two developers editing the same rule overwrite each other's changes.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Who manages the project scope and prioritizes requirements in sprints so each release delivers business value?

options.text: The Product Owner (PO)
The Scrum Master
The Lead System Architect
The UX Designer

practiceQuiz.hint: Managing scope and prioritizing sprint requirements defines the Product Owner role.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The PO manages scope and prioritizes requirements per sprint. B is wrong because the Scrum Master facilitates ceremonies and removes impediments. C configures the app/imports Blueprint. D focuses on UI/accessibility.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which role facilitates Sprint Planning, Sizing, Backlog Refinement, and Retrospectives and removes impediments?

options.text: The Scrum Master
The Project Manager
The Product Owner
The Subject Matter Expert

practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the Scrum role responsible for facilitating ceremonies and removing team impediments.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Scrum Master runs Scrum ceremonies and removes impediments. Project Manager (B) maintains governance and schedule. Product Owner (C) prioritizes scope. Subject Matter Expert (D) supplies operational requirements.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Who is responsible for importing Blueprint files into Pega Platform and configuring functional and technical requirements from user stories?

options.text: The Lead System Architect (LSA)
The Business Architect
The Quality Analyst
The Solutions Consultant

practiceQuiz.hint: Which team role is responsible for importing Blueprint files into Pega Platform?
practiceQuiz.rationale: The LSA imports Blueprint files and configures functional/technical requirements. B translates needs into workflows/Data Models. C writes tests. D co-designs the Blueprint early in sales but does not import it into the platform.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which role engages the client early in the sales process and co-designs the Blueprint before handing it to the delivery team?

options.text: The Solutions Consultant
The Project Manager
The Scrum Master
The Quality Analyst

practiceQuiz.hint: Which role engages the client during pre-sales and co-designs the Blueprint before delivery?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Solutions Consultant engages the client early in the sales cycle and co-designs the Blueprint. The other roles (B/C/D) are all delivery-phase roles who join after the engagement is sold.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A new Pega project team is being onboarded and the project lead needs to determine which team members require access to Dev Studio for their day-to-day development and configuration work. Which TWO roles in a Pega project primarily use Dev Studio?

options.text: System Architects
Quality Analysts
Data scientists
Business-related IT administrators

practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the two roles whose primary workspace is Dev Studio for technical build and test work.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Dev Studio is the workspace for technical members — System Architects and Quality Analysts. Prediction Studio (C) serves data scientists. Admin Studio (D) serves system administrators.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is explaining Pega's parallel development approach to a team that must build three independent features simultaneously without their changes colliding. A developer asks how their personal development environment is isolated from teammates. What is a Workspace in Pega parallel development?

options.text: A secure space tied to ONE operator and ONE application; changes stay private until shared to a Branch
A shared team area where all developers' changes are immediately visible to everyone
A versioned container of released application features
A Work Queue for development tasks

practiceQuiz.hint: A Workspace is private, tied to one operator and exactly one application.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A Workspace is private to one operator and one application; changes are private until shared to a Branch. B is wrong because Workspace changes are private, not immediately shared. C describes the application. D is unrelated.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How many Workspaces can an operator have within an application, and how are Workspaces turned on?

options.text: One by default, but the operator can create multiple; Workspaces are enabled with the EnableWorkspace setting
Exactly one, always; they are on by default and cannot be disabled
Unlimited and shared across applications; no setting is required
One per Work Group; enabled in Admin Studio

practiceQuiz.hint: Default is one Workspace per operator; multiple allowed; EnableWorkspace setting required.
practiceQuiz.rationale: An operator has one Workspace by default but can create multiple per application; Workspaces are enabled via EnableWorkspace. B is wrong because multiple are allowed. C is wrong because a Workspace is tied to one application. D is wrong because Workspaces are per operator, not per Work Group.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Pega project team is about to develop three features in parallel. The SA recommends that each feature be developed in its own Branch Ruleset. A junior developer who is unfamiliar with the concept asks for a definition. What is a Branch Ruleset in Pega Platform?

options.text: A Ruleset that is based on (branched from) another Ruleset and holds the Rules in active development in that Branch
A standalone Ruleset with no relationship to any other Ruleset
A Ruleset that stores only released, generally available Rules
A copy of the entire application database

practiceQuiz.hint: Branch Rulesets are based on another Ruleset and hold currently in-development Rules.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A Branch Ruleset is branched from another Ruleset and contains the Branch's in-development Rules. B is wrong because it is based on another Ruleset. C describes released Rules in the main app. D is unrelated.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A junior SA asks a senior team lead when a development Branch in Pega can be merged back into the main application Ruleset. Under what conditions does a Branch qualify to merge into the main application?

options.text: Only after the feature is complete, conflicts are resolved, and approval is granted
Immediately and automatically as soon as any Rule is changed in the Branch
Only when all other Branches are also complete
Never — Branches cannot be merged, only deleted

practiceQuiz.hint: Recall the three conditions that must all be true before a Branch can be merged into the main application.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A Branch merges only after the feature is complete, conflicts are resolved, and approval is granted. B is wrong because merging is deliberate, not automatic on every change. C is wrong because Branches merge independently. D is wrong because merging is the whole point of Branches.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A team wants to check, before merging, how many of their Branch Rules are covered by tests. Which Branch quality metric shows this?

options.text: Test coverage / Unit tests — e.g., the Rules covered and Test pass rate metrics
The Weighted score guardrail metric
Total merge conflicts
Uncovered Rules only — there is no coverage percentage

practiceQuiz.rationale: Test coverage and Unit tests metrics (Rules covered %, Test pass rate %) show how much of the Branch is tested. B reflects guardrail warnings. C counts conflicts. D counts untested Rules but is not the coverage percentage.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A team lead is reviewing a development Branch before approving it for merge. Which TWO are Branch quality metrics that Pega uses to judge whether a Branch is ready to merge?

options.text: Guardrails (Weighted score) — number and severity of best-practice warnings
Merge conflicts (Total merge conflicts) — potential conflicts to resolve
Operator Urgency — the priority of the developer's worklist
Ruleset lock count — how many Rulesets are locked

practiceQuiz.hint: Which two Branch quality metrics are used to assess whether a Branch is ready to merge?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Guardrails (Weighted score) and Merge conflicts (Total conflicts) are both documented Branch quality metrics. The other options (C and D) are not tracked as Branch quality metrics in Pega.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A developer creates a Locations Data Object in their own space and verifies it before letting teammates see it, then promotes it for the team. What is the correct promotion path?

options.text: Workspace (private) → Branch (team) → Application (released)
Application → Branch → Workspace
Branch → Workspace → Application
Workspace → Application directly, skipping the Branch

practiceQuiz.hint: Match the three development progression stages to the three Pega workspace types in sequence.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Changes flow Workspace (private) → Branch (team) → Application (released). B reverses the flow. C is wrong about ordering. D skips the team-sharing Branch step.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Pega project includes System Architects, Business Architects, and developers working in parallel. Which TWO statements correctly describe how roles align with the Pega development environment?

options.text: System Architects primarily use Dev Studio to configure low-level technical Rules and advanced configurations
Business Architects primarily use App Studio to configure Case Types, data models, and UI without requiring Dev Studio access
All team members must use Dev Studio for any Rule configuration — App Studio is view-only and cannot edit Rules
Business Architects and System Architects use identical studios with the same feature sets and no difference in access

practiceQuiz.hint: SA = Dev Studio for technical depth; BA = App Studio for business configuration without code.
practiceQuiz.rationale: System Architects use Dev Studio for technical Rule configuration including advanced rule types, inheritance, and debugging. Business Architects primarily use App Studio, which provides a no-code interface for configuring Case Types, data objects, and UI. App Studio is fully functional for editing — it is not view-only.

SA/SSA/LSA (LSA imports Blueprint) · QA (scenario tests) · BA (workflows/Data Model/UX).

App (most + PM docs + Scrum user stories) · Dev (SAs/QAs) · Prediction (data scientists) · Admin (IT).
